newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Continuing its practice, the finance ministry will release a new list of those found to be contravening the tax code. The names this time, however, will not be of firms and individuals evading taxes but of tax officials found complicit in tax evasion. At the same time, another 460 firms and a range of ailing firms and subsidised agencies are coming under the microscope.
--Some 40,000 customers will be be able to breathe easier after Housing Bank decided to offer the option of renegotiating previously high interest rates.
--Greek telecoms organisation OTE's book-building price/share was set at 6,200-6,900 drachmas yesterday, the National Bank announced.

--OTE prices are settling at ranges higher than previously expected and the market sees profits in the second OTE share offer, following the setting of book-building prices yesterday. OTE shares on the Athens bourse yesterday settled at 7,105 drachmas.
--Two finalists - the Latsis Group and Piraeus Bank - will battle it out for Cretabank following their selection yesterday to the shortlist for the sale of the state-run bank.

--Part-time work should be increased and supported and local sector agreements should be allowed to be drafted in regions which are chronically industrially depressed, OECD tells the Greek government.
--There is talk of constructing a fuel pipeline from Skopje to Thessaloniki, with Mamidaki Brothers Group, Jetoil Enterprises and entrepreneurs from Skopje showing active interest in the project.
--The modification of software and software systems to the new needs demanded by economic and monetary union (EMU) could cost commercial banks up to 300 billion drachmas, according to sources.
--The European Union's economy and finance ministers reiterated yesterday their stable commitment to Maastricht criteria for member-states to move to the third phase of economic and monetary union.

--There will be far-reaching institutional reforms to the pension and social security system by the end of 1998, Prime Minister Costas Simitis announced in Parliament yesterday. the reforms will be implemented in two stages. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
